records.summary: 1801 Haight St is an existing restaurant with an active ABC Type 47 license (full bar) that has operated continuously since at least 1992. The address is zoned NCD-HAIGHT where restaurants are principally permitted on the first story, but it sits within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict which requires Conditional Use for any new on-sale liquor establishment. The restaurant currently holds a Type 47 license issued in June 2024 following a complex license history including Type 41, Type 75, Type 06/74 craft distillery licenses. The immediate block is extremely dense: 19 food/drink businesses and 8 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, with five bars in that radius. Because the concept enlarges an existing restaurant that already holds a Type 47 license, it appears to be a continuation of use rather than establishing a new liquor establishment, consistent with Planning's 2024 interpretation for the current license.

comparables.why_comparable: Same address (1801 Haight St, 15m), same existing restaurant, approved Type 47 license transfer in May 2024. Agency referral for ABC Type 47 within the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved the current Type 47 as a continuation of existing use in the Haight RUSD, finding that prior Type 06/74 craft distillery licenses were similar to Type 47, so no CUA was required. This established that the restaurant's alcohol service is grandfathered, directly supporting the current outdoor expansion.

comparables.why_comparable: Same address (1801 Haight St, 15m), approved CUA in 1992 to expand this non-conforming restaurant from 820 sq ft to 2,270 sq ft in the Haight Street NCD. Use decision by Planning Commission.
comparables.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a major expansion of this restaurant 33 years ago, establishing precedent that enlargement of an existing restaurant at this site is appropriate. The concept has operated continuously since, suggesting operational compatibility with the neighborhood.

comparables.why_comparable: Outdoor dining for existing restaurant at 1650-1654 Haight St (230m west, same NCD-HAIGHT district). Required both CUA and Variance (separate case 2007.1046V). Use decisions approved January 2008.
comparables.key_takeaway: Outdoor dining on Haight Street required a Conditional Use Authorization (not just over-the-counter approval), taking 4 months from filing to CUA approval. The variance was filed 3 months after the CUA and approved 12 days later, suggesting technical rear-yard or setback issues common to this corridor.

comparables.why_comparable: Outdoor seating for existing restaurant at 1640 Haight St (247m west, same NCD-HAIGHT district). Agency referral approved May 2013 as continuation of use under prior CUA cases.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning permitted outdoor seating as a continuation of existing restaurant use citing prior CUA language (CU80.096 and 1988.341V), with the explicit condition that no building expansion or lightwell infill was allowed. This suggests outdoor seating tied to historical approvals may be handled administratively rather than requiring new CUA.

comparables.why_comparable: Limited Live Performance permit with outdoor entertainment and amplified sound in a parklet at 1807 Haight St (24m away, same block, NCD-HAIGHT district). Entertainment Commission referral approved June 2024.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning approved outdoor entertainment in a parklet at the bar next door just 8 months ago, confirming that outdoor use expansions on this block are currently viewed favorably. The proximity (24m) and recency are strong positive signals for outdoor dining at 1801.

comparables.why_comparable: ABC Type 41 transfer for existing restaurant at 1790 Haight St (53m across the street, NCD-HAIGHT). Agency referral approved August 2022 for continuation of existing liquor establishment in Haight RUSD.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning routinely approves ABC license transfers for existing restaurants in the Haight RUSD under the continuation-of-use exception (PC §781.9(c)(4)), even with eight on-sale licenses within 500 ft. Since this concept already holds a Type 47, outdoor expansion should not trigger new liquor-establishment review.

comparables.why_comparable: Change of use from movie house to restaurant at 1721-1737 Haight St (68m east, NCD-HAIGHT). CUA approved October 2012 after 6-month review.
comparables.key_takeaway: A major change of use to restaurant on this corridor required CUA and took 6 months, but was approved, showing that the Commission supports restaurant density on Haight Street even in the NCD district.

patterns.pattern: Outdoor seating for existing restaurants in NCD-HAIGHT has been consistently approved, but the permit path varies: some required full CUA (2007.1046C took 4 months), while others were approved as agency referrals citing continuation of use under prior CUA language (MB1300620 took 5 weeks).

Planning interprets the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict's CUA requirement (PC §781.9) to apply only to NEW on-sale liquor establishments. Existing restaurants with active ABC licenses—even through transfer or license-type changes—are approved as continuation of use without CUA.

At 1801 Haight St specifically, Planning has approved two expansions of the restaurant over 33 years (1992.148C expanded from 820 to 2,270 sq ft; 2023-010501MIS approved Type 47 license), establishing that enlargement of this long-operating use is acceptable.

Outdoor dining approvals on Haight Street sometimes carry conditions prohibiting building expansion or infill (MB1300620 explicitly stated 'no building expansion or lightwell infill'), suggesting DBI and Planning scrutinize whether outdoor structures encroach on required yards or alter building footprints.

Recent approvals (2024-004523MIS for outdoor entertainment next door, 2023-010501MIS for the Type 47 at this address) show that Planning currently views expansions of existing food/drink uses on this block favorably, including outdoor components.

Multiple ABC license transfers and continuations in the Haight RUSD have been approved administratively as agency referrals (2022-007085MIS, 2022-008240MIS, 2023-010501MIS) without requiring Planning Commission hearings, even in a high-density area with 8 on-sale licenses within 500 ft.

risk.concept_summary: Enlargement of an existing restaurant at 1801 Haight St by adding outdoor dining in the parking lot, with limited cooking, alcohol service, tenant improvements for restroom and exit signage, and five employees.

overall.next_step: Confirm in writing with San Francisco Planning whether the outdoor dining area meets all limits of Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) for principally permitted outdoor activity areas, or whether a Conditional Use Authorization is required for this enlargement.

approvals.summary: Enlarging the existing restaurant requires Conditional Use Authorization per Planning Code § 178 because a new restaurant would be conditional in the Haight Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict and the records do not establish whether the outdoor area meets all principally permitted limits.

findings.text: An active ABC Type 47 licence (full bar, eating place) is on file at 1801 Haight St, issued June 6, 2024, and the rules read the space as a Restaurant from that licence type.

Planning approved the current Type 47 licence in May 2024 as a continuation of existing use in the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict, finding that prior Type 06 and Type 74 craft distillery licences were similar to a Type 47, so no new on-sale liquor establishment was created.
A Conditional Use Authorization approved in May 1992 expanded this restaurant from 820 sq ft to 2,270 sq ft at 1801 Haight St, establishing precedent for enlargement at this address.

The Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict requires Conditional Use for new on-sale liquor establishments (ABC Types 40, 41, 42, 47, 48, 57), and a new restaurant here would require Conditional Use under that rule even though restaurants are principally permitted in NCD-HAIGHT zoning.

Planning Code § 178 prohibits significantly altering, enlarging or intensifying a conditional use without a new Conditional Use Authorization, and enlarging an existing restaurant that would be conditional if new triggers this requirement.

The records do not establish whether the outdoor area meets every limit of Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) for principally permitted outdoor activity areas: on the ground level; operating only 9 a.m. to 10 p.m.; not with a Bar use; seated only with no standing; alcohol dispensed only inside or by wait staff at the seat.

approvals.summary: The concept states it already holds the alcohol licence, but the description does not specify whether beer and wine or full liquor will be served, so the rules cannot determine which ABC licence type applies or whether Planning Code liquor-district rules are met.

findings.text: The business states it already holds the alcohol licence. An active ABC Type 47 (on-sale general, eating place) is on file at 1801 Haight St, issued June 6, 2024.
Eight active on-sale ABC licences exist within 500 ft of this address, and 18 within 1,000 ft, triggering the density statistics' undue-concentration flag as a proxy for ABC's census tract test.

Planning approved three ABC licence transfers or continuations for existing restaurants in the Haight Street Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict within 100 meters of this address between August 2022 and May 2024, all as continuation of existing liquor establishments without requiring Conditional Use Authorization.

Six health-permit agency referrals for restaurants at 1801 Haight St and adjacent addresses on this parcel were approved between 2010 and 2024, most within 10 to 20 days, as continuation of existing restaurant use.

expected_conditions.condition: Outdoor dining hours limited to 9:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. if the outdoor area is to be principally permitted under Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7).
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) permits outdoor activity areas without Conditional Use only if they operate between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. The 2013 approval at 1640 Haight St cited this section for outdoor seating as a continuation of use, and the 2008 outdoor dining CUA at 1650 Haight St likely carried hour limits as well.

expected_conditions.condition: Alcohol service outdoors limited to seated patrons only, with alcohol dispensed inside the premises or by wait staff at the patron's seat; no self-service bar or standing drink areas outdoors.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) permits outdoor activity areas with a Restaurant only if alcohol is dispensed inside or by wait staff at the seat. The Haight Alcohol Restricted Use Subdistrict's sensitivity to new alcohol establishments suggests any outdoor alcohol service will be scrutinized.

expected_conditions.condition: Outdoor seating area limited to seated dining only; no standing areas, loitering or congregation space outdoors.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) allows outdoor activity areas with a Restaurant only for seated areas with no standing. This is a standard condition to distinguish restaurant outdoor dining from bar-style outdoor areas.

expected_conditions.condition: The outdoor structure may not alter the building footprint, encroach on required rear yards under Planning Code § 134, or constitute building expansion that would require neighborhood notification or discretionary review.
expected_conditions.basis: The 2013 approval at 1640 Haight St explicitly conditioned outdoor seating on 'no building expansion or lightwell infill.' Planning and DBI scrutinize whether outdoor structures in parking lots or rear yards comply with setback rules.

expected_conditions.condition: The business must continue to operate as a bona fide eating place, with food service available during all hours alcohol is served, per Planning Code § 790.142.
expected_conditions.basis: Multiple ABC referrals for restaurants in the Haight Street district (2017-007014MIS, 2017-007731MIS, MB1300289) were conditioned on operating as a bona fide eating place to maintain the restaurant use rather than becoming a bar use.

expected_conditions.condition: Compliance with all conditions of the 1992 Conditional Use Authorization (case 1992.148C) unless explicitly modified by a new CUA or written determination from Planning.
expected_conditions.basis: Planning Code § 303(e) requires a new Conditional Use Authorization to change the conditions of an earlier approval. The 1992 CUA is on file for this address, and the rules flagged that whether the proposal changes its conditions is not established.

filing_playbook.action: Schedule a pre-application meeting with San Francisco Planning to confirm whether the outdoor dining area meets all limits of Planning Code § 202.2(a)(7) or requires a Conditional Use Authorization.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Present the parking-lot location, proposed hours (request confirmation whether 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. is acceptable), seating plan (no standing areas), and alcohol service method (served by wait staff at tables only, not self-service). Ask whether this is a principally permitted outdoor activity area or requires CUA under § 178 as an enlargement. Request a written Letter of Determination or email confirmation before filing any applications.

filing_playbook.action: If Planning confirms a Conditional Use Authorization is required, prepare and file a CUA application with San Francisco Planning, including a project description, site plan, seating layout, hours of operation, alcohol service plan, and neighbor outreach documentation.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Frame the proposal as an enlargement of a long-established restaurant (operating since at least 1992, previously approved for expansion under case 1992.148C) that improves the outdoor dining character of Haight Street. Emphasize that the existing ABC Type 47 licence continues without establishing a new on-sale liquor establishment, consistent with Planning's May 2024 interpretation in case 2023-010501MIS. Commit to hours ending by 10 p.m., seated service only, and alcohol served by wait staff at tables. Highlight that the adjacent bar at 1807 Haight St was approved for outdoor entertainment in a parklet in June 2024, showing current Planning support for outdoor uses on this block.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN), required before any other city permit applications.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File online or in person with the entity name, federal EIN, and business address. The BAN is needed for the health plan check, building permit, and any Planning applications.

filing_playbook.action: Submit building permit plans to the SF Department of Building Inspection for the tenant improvements (raised outdoor structure, new restroom, exit signage), with architectural plans stamped by a California-licensed architect.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Include the site plan showing the parking-lot outdoor dining area, structural details of any raised platform, restroom and exit upgrades, and confirmation that no building footprint expansion or rear-yard encroachment occurs. Request routing to Planning (automatic under PC § 175(a)) and DPH. Attach the Letter of Determination or CUA approval from step 1 or 2 to show zoning compliance for the outdoor area.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check application for the kitchen and outdoor dining area through the SF Department of Public Health Environmental Health portal, including menu, equipment list, seating layout, and finishes schedule.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Describe limited cooking (the concept states limited cooking type), the outdoor dining area as an extension of the existing restaurant, and any new handwash or prep sinks. Request a pre-final inspection at 80% construction completion and schedule the final pre-opening inspection at least two weeks in advance with the assigned plan reviewer.

filing_playbook.action: If the existing ABC Type 47 licence premises does not already include the outdoor area, file a premises modification application with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control to add the parking-lot dining area to the licensed premises.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Attach a diagram showing the indoor and outdoor service areas, the CUA or Letter of Determination from Planning approving the outdoor area, and confirmation that alcohol will be served only by wait staff at seated patrons' tables. ABC may require a 30-day public posting and local agency sign-off.

filing_playbook.action: After DBI issues the building permit and DPH approves the plans, complete construction and request the final DPH pre-opening inspection, with a certified food safety manager on staff and the DPH-approved plans on site.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Confirm all equipment, finishes, handwash sinks, and the outdoor dining area match the approved plans. The health permit to operate is issued after the final inspection passes.

timeline_cost.notes: This range is the time to approval if the Conditional Use Authorization and building permit are granted. It covers the CUA (120–300 days from filing to Commission approval per the 2007 outdoor dining case at 1650 Haight St and typical CUA timelines) and the building permit (14–120 days). The CUA is the critical path: pre-application meetings and preparation add 4–8 weeks before filing, environmental review and neighborhood notification add 60–90 days, and hearing scheduling takes another 30–60 days. If Planning determines at the pre-application meeting that the outdoor area is principally permitted under PC § 202.2(a)(7), the timeline drops to 14–120 days for the building permit and health permit only (submitted in parallel), and the cost drops to $800–$15,000 building permit plus $1,298–$3,500 health plan check and permit, totaling roughly $2,100–$18,500. The cost range shown assumes a CUA is required: approximately $3,100–$15,000 for a CUA (depending on construction valuation and fee waiver eligibility, based on catalog entry for sf.conditional_use_authorization) plus $800–$15,000 building permit, excluding the health permit fees already included in other approvals. These figures are government fees only and exclude architect, expediter, and construction costs. The outdoor dining cases at 1650 Haight St took 128 days (CUA filed Sept 2007, approved Jan 2008) plus 12 days for the variance, and at 1640 Haight St took 36 days (agency referral filed April 2013, approved May 2013), showing the wide range depending on the permit path.
